content: Chinese DRAM maker CXMT rejected Apple's attempt to negotiate prices below Samsung and SK Hynix levels. CXMT's capacity is already locked by long-term contracts with domestic clients like Huawei and Xiaomi. The reversal reflects shifting power dynamics: AI demand has tightened traditional DRAM supply, raising prices 350-490%, while CXMT's technology gap with Korean rivals has narrowed to minimal levels. Apple previously used supplier competition and Chinese vendors as leverage, but alternative options are dwindling as memory makers prioritize higher-margin AI chips. Chinese semiconductor firms are transitioning from low-cost substitutes to equal partners with pricing power.
